statement:
Let $\mathrm{Cov}_{\mathcal C}$ denote the covering families of a site. In this lemma the coefficient diagram $i\mapsto\mathcal F_i$ consists of **abelian sheaves**, despite the more general ringed-site discussion earlier in the section. A cofinal collection of coverings of $U$ means every covering admits refinement by one in the collection. The canonical comparison $\operatorname{colim}_i H^p(U,\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(U,\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal F_i)$ comes from the compatible maps into the sheaf colimit.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$ be the set
of coverings of $\mathcal{C}$ (see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-site}). Let
$\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ with $I$ finite,
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then the map
$$
\colim_i H^p(U, \mathcal{F}_i)
\longrightarrow
H^p(U, \colim_i \mathcal{F}_i)
$$
is an isomorphism for every $p \geq 0$, every $U \in \mathcal{B}$, and
every filtered diagram $\mathcal{I} \to \textit{Ab}(\mathcal{C})$.
hypotheses: $\mathcal C$ is a site; $\mathcal B\subseteq\mathrm{Ob}(\mathcal C)$, and $\mathrm{Cov}$ is a selected set of coverings.
Every covering in $\mathrm{Cov}$ is indexed by a **finite** set $I$, its target, all its members and their finite iterated fibre products lie in $\mathcal B$.
For every $U\in\mathcal B$, the coverings of $U$ in $\mathrm{Cov}$ are cofinal.
$i\mapsto\mathcal F_i$ is a **filtered** diagram of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: For every $p\ge0$ and $U\in\mathcal B$, the natural map $\operatorname{colim}_iH^p(U,\mathcal F_i)\to H^p(U,\operatorname{colim}_i\mathcal F_i)$ is an isomorphism.

statement:
For a morphism of sites $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ corresponding to a continuous functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, the sheaf $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal D$ is obtained by sheafification of $V\mapsto H^p(u(V),\mathcal F)$ (for abelian sheaves). Let $\mathcal F=\operatorname{colim}\mathcal F_i$ denote the colimit in abelian sheaves, and let $\mathcal B$ consist precisely of objects $V$ of $\mathcal D$ for which the specified degree-$p$ cohomology commutes with this colimit.

Let $f : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a morphism of sites
corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of
abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$. Set $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$.
Let $p \geq 0$ be an integer. Denote $\mathcal{B}$ the set of
$V \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ such that
$H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}) = \colim H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}_i)$.
If every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
then $R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = \colim R^pf_*\mathcal{F}_i$.
hypotheses: $f:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is a morphism of sites induced by continuous $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$.
$(\mathcal F_i,\varphi_{ii'})$ is a filtered direct system of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal F=\operatorname{colim}\mathcal F_i$.
Every $V\in\mathcal D$ has a covering by objects of $\mathcal B$.
conclusions: The canonical morphism $\operatorname{colim}_i R^p f_*\mathcal F_i\to R^pf_*\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves on $\mathcal D$.

\label{lemma-higher-direct-image-colimit}
Let $f : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$ be a morphism of sites
corresponding to the continuous functor $u : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$.
Let $(\mathcal{F}_i, \varphi_{ii'})$ be a system of
abelian sheaves on $\mathcal{C}$. Set $\mathcal{F} = \colim \mathcal{F}_i$.
Let $p \geq 0$ be an integer. Denote $\mathcal{B}$ the set of
$V \in \Ob(\mathcal{D})$ such that
$H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}) = \colim H^p(u(V), \mathcal{F}_i)$.
If every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by elements of $\mathcal{B}$,
then $R^pf_*\mathcal{F} = \colim R^pf_*\mathcal{F}_i$.
